n: Intermediate Value Theorem: f continuous on [a, b] and K between f(a) and f(b) ⇒ some c in (a, b) has f(c) = K. It is why bisection works. Taylor: f(x) = Pₙ(x) + Rₙ(x), Rₙ(x) = f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(ξ)(x − x₀)ⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1)!

k-digit chopping drops extra digits; rounding rounds the k-th digit. Absolute error |p − p*|; relative error |p − p*| / |p|. Exam trap Relative error divides by the TRUE value p, not the approximation.
Subtracting nearly equal numbers loses significant digits; rewrite the formula (e.g. rationalize) to avoid it.

Bisection: pₙ = (aₙ + bₙ)/2; keep the half where f changes sign. Always converges (slowly, linearly). Tip Error bound: |pₙ − p| ≤ (b − a)/2ⁿ. To reach tolerance ε, need n ≥ log₂((b − a)/ε).

Newton: pₙ = pₙ₋₁ − f(pₙ₋₁)/f′(pₙ₋₁). Quadratic convergence near a simple root, but needs f′ and a good starting point.
Secant: replaces f′ with the slope through the last two points: pₙ = pₙ₋₁ − f(pₙ₋₁)(pₙ₋₁ − pₙ₋₂)/(f(pₙ₋₁) − f(pₙ₋₂)). No derivative needed.

False position: secant formula but keeps the two points that bracket the root (like bisection), so it always converges. Memory trick Newton needs f′; secant drops f′; false position = secant + bracketing.

Order α: |pₙ₊₁ − p| / |pₙ − p|^α → λ. α = 1 linear, α = 2 quadratic.
At a multiple root Newton is only linear; modified Newton uses μ = f/f′: pₙ = pₙ₋₁ − f f′/((f′)² − f f″).

Aitken's Δ²: p̂ₙ = pₙ − (pₙ₊₁ − pₙ)² / (pₙ₊₂ − 2pₙ₊₁ + pₙ).
Steffensen: apply Aitken to fixed-point iterates every third step: quadratic convergence without derivatives.

Lagrange: P(x) = Σ f(xₖ)Lₖ(x), Lₖ(x) = Π_{i≠k} (x − xᵢ)/(xₖ − xᵢ). Degree ≤ n through n + 1 points. Error: f(x) − P(x) = f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(ξ)/(n + 1)! · Π(x − xᵢ).

Neville: Q_{i,j} = ((x − x_{i−j})Q_{i,j−1} − (x − xᵢ)Q_{i−1,j−1}) / (xᵢ − x_{i−j}). Good for evaluating P at ONE x.

f[xᵢ, xᵢ₊₁] = (f[xᵢ₊₁] − f[xᵢ])/(xᵢ₊₁ − xᵢ), and so on. Pₙ(x) = f[x₀] + f[x₀, x₁](x − x₀) + f[x₀, x₁, x₂](x − x₀)(x − x₁) + … Memory trick Adding a new point only adds one new term: no need to start over (unlike Lagrange).
Equally spaced nodes: forward differences Δ and the binomial-coefficient form.

Cubic spline: Sⱼ(x) = aⱼ + bⱼ(x − xⱼ) + cⱼ(x − xⱼ)² + dⱼ(x − xⱼ)³ on each subinterval; S, S′, S″ continuous.
Natural spline: S″(x₀) = S″(xₙ) = 0.
Clamped spline: S′(x₀) = f′(x₀), S′(xₙ) = f′(xₙ) (usually more accurate).

Three-point endpoint: f′(x₀) ≈ (−3f(x₀) + 4f(x₀ + h) − f(x₀ + 2h))/(2h).
Three-point midpoint: f′(x₀) ≈ (f(x₀ + h) − f(x₀ − h))/(2h), error O(h²).
Second derivative midpoint: f″(x₀) ≈ (f(x₀ − h) − 2f(x₀) + f(x₀ + h))/h².
